todos.item: End-to-end noisy-channel tokenizer at tc512: fold z + σ·ε into training with the encoder in the graph
todos.note: ../research/plan/2026-09-07_tc_width_decnoise_e2e_tc512.md. Submitted 2026-09-07 as BSC:45529827. Routed here by falsifier 3 of TODO 12's plan: *"the pair needs a from-scratch noisy tokenizer, which changes z and is a tc_width/sigreg question, not a flow one."* One arm — copy of slurm/deltatok/train_deltatok_compose_sigreg_nozn_tc512_bsc.slurm with model.deltatok.decode_noise_tau=0.8 · training.decode_noise_warmup=2000 · training.eval_noise_sigmas=[0.32,0.55,0.82], RUN_NAME=..._compose1.0_decnoise0.8, 100 ep at 0.61 h/ep measured on the twin → ~61 h; shipped at 40 h a job per the BSC backfill convention, so it needs one chained resume. Unlike TODO 12 the encoder is not frozen: the add is differentiable, so the encoder optimises a code that must survive the channel, while SIGReg and the compose sum keep reading the clean z. Two new knobs (the τ ramp, and the tokenizer's own noise ladder as an [Eval/…] scalar — no tc512 flow checkpoint exists, so the ladder cannot be read the way TODO 12 read it) plus an eval-only job on the twin's epoch_80.pth for the "before" ladder. Control BSC:45296347 at matched ep 40 / 72 / 80. Tripwire at ep 12. Motivation: the cov_weight dose-response (TODO 6) shows train ZPartRank monotone in dose to 141.0 with none of it transferring to recon, so a term that pushes E[zzᵀ]→I is answered; a noisy channel applies the pressure through the reconstruction loss instead

todos.item: Attack the rank ceiling directly instead of via the weight
todos.note: done: results/2026-09-06_sigreg_cov_penalty_tc512_slides.html. Four doses over one base (tc512 · compose 1.0 · sigreg 0.02): cov 0 BSC:45296347, 3e-5 BSC:45416718 (ep 72, 44 h wall), 1e-4 BSC:45498520 and 3e-4 BSC:45498521 (both cancelled 2026-09-07 at ep 29/100, 18 h of 44 h — the axis was already answered). Verdict: not worth adding. cov_weight does exactly what it was designed to do to the spectrum and almost nothing to reconstruction. Train ZPartRank is monotone in dose with no ceiling — 84.8 → 109.1 → 115.8 → 163.3 at matched ep 29, a 1.9× spread — while eval LossRecon moves a few percent and not even in dose order: on the ep 24–29 mean only 3e-5 is ahead of the control (−10.6% K / −10.6% N), 1e-4 is behind it (+8.0% / +5.3%) and 3e-4 clears the control (−6.1% / −4.9%) but not 3e-5 (+5.0% / +6.4%). This falsifies the thread's central hypothesis: participation rank is not the lever on reconstruction. The r = −0.997 … −0.999 rank↔recon correlation that motivated the term held across arms that differed in convergence, and it breaks the moment rank is pushed directly at a fixed recipe — 1.9× the rank buys nothing. Rank stays a diagnostic, never a target. No dose reached the 0.0528 K / 0.0370 N weight-axis best either, so the plateau confound of TODO 2 is not settled and was not settled by this route. Left open: slides 1–10 of the deck still carry the earlier ep-67 3e-5 reading ("a new best, narrowly") and disagree with slide 11 — the ep-29 dose axis is the one to quote. §4–5 of plan/2026-09-02_sigreg_cov_penalty.md were written under the old reading and carry a reversal note. Both cancelled current.pth are resumable at ep 29 if the axis is ever revisited; the 3e-4 late-crossing question is dropped, not measured.
